subject: Day 61: respond to his name
bodyText:
Today's focus
Around now Avi begins turning attention toward his own name and holding back-and-forth coo exchanges. The week's job is to feed that reciprocity, since conversational turns, not raw word count, are what predict later language outcomes.

Action items
- Say his name warmly during awake-alert windows and watch for the orienting turn; then respond to each coo as if he spoke, pause two to three seconds, and answer again. Conversational turns drive Broca's-area development independent of total word count. Romeo et al. 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Confirm the 4-month visit is scheduled, window day 112-126, where RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, and IPV #2 are due; the rotavirus series has hard age cutoffs, so do not let it drift. AAP immunization policy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/immunizations/aap-policy-on-immunizations/
- Start a loose first-birthday plan now if you want a specific SF or NYC venue, since top venues book six to nine months out and putting the date down prevents calendar collisions with family visits.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Quiet startle to loud sounds and wet sneezing during the day; both are routine and need no action.
- [monitor] No social smile by this point; note it and raise it at the next well visit rather than waiting.
- [call within 24h] A run of refused feeds in a row, or new color changes during feeds.
- [call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher under 90 days, an apnea pause, or seizure-like activity needs a call now, and 911 for blue lips or labored breathing.

Enrichment opportunities
- Use his name and warm parentese in serve-and-return turns, pausing for his reply; back-and-forth cooing is consolidating and the turn-taking is the active ingredient, not the volume. Romeo et al. 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Vary the tummy-time surface across the day, a firm mat, your lap, then a slight Boppy incline, to keep cumulative prone time above 60 minutes and build neck and upper-body strength. AAP tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Take a carrier walk outside with his chin off his chest and face visible, giving him upright sensory input and the parent some cardiovascular recovery. AAP movement guide: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-Birth-to-Three-Months.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 57-72 (now): tail of the post-vaccine window; lingering low-grade fussiness is still expected.
- Day 84-91: sleep-consolidation window opens near three months; start anchoring a consistent sleep-wake routine.
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit, with RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, and IPV #2.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete

- Turns head toward the sound of your voice
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Localizes sound source. Worth raising with the pediatrician if absent at the 4-month visit.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/turns-head-toward-sound/complete

- Makes sounds back when you talk to him
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Conversational turn-taking. Foundation for later vocabulary growth.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/makes-sounds-back/complete

- Opens mouth when she sees the breast or bottle
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Anticipatory recognition — feeding is now associated with the sight, not just the sensation.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/opens-mouth-for-breast/complete
